subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bold part of the sentence.

The man is blind **of** **one eye.**
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"blind of one eye"** is grammatically incorrect and not used in standard English.
 
• The correct preposition to use with "blind" in this context is **"with"**, not "of," "by," or "from."
 
• The standard and idiomatic expression is **"blind with one eye"**, meaning a person cannot see from one of their eyes.
 
• Therefore, the improved sentence is **"The man is blind with one eye."**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The man is blind with one eye."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **with one eye** – Correct usage; means the person has sight in only one eye.
 
• **by one eye** – Incorrect; “by” doesn’t fit grammatically in this context.
 
• **on one eye** – Incorrect; “on” suggests physical placement, not ability.
 
• **from one eye** – Incorrect; not idiomatic in English for describing blindness.
